rows.grounds: pronoun referring to the supreme soul

items.question: What is the true nature of the supreme soul that is partless eternal and stainless?
premises: The supreme soul is free from disease and stainless.
items.inference: The supreme soul is described as partless, eternal, and stainless.
uncertainties: The exact syntactic relation of paraṃ to saḥ is not fully explicit.
items.plain_english: He is supreme, partless, eternal, free from disease, and stainless.

items.question: Who is the supreme soul identified as haṃsa composed of power and individual?
premises: The soul is identified as haṃsa.
Haṃsa is described as power plus individual.
items.inference: The supreme soul is identified with haṃsa, the power-individual.
uncertainties: The exact force of parataro as comparative is not fully resolved.
items.plain_english: He is the soul, supreme indeed; he is haṃsa, power and individual.

items.question: Where is the wind-filled air situated among all beings?
premises: The air is situated in all beings.
items.inference: The wind-filled air is situated in all beings.
uncertainties: The exact relation of samīra+pūrako to vāyuḥ is not fully explicit.
items.plain_english: The wind-filled air is situated in all beings.

items.question: What is the soul called upon merely leaving the body?
premises: Upon merely leaving the body, he is called supreme.
items.inference: Upon merely leaving the body, the soul is called supreme Śiva.
uncertainties: The exact scope of mātreṇa is not fully explicit.
items.plain_english: Upon merely leaving the body, he is called supreme Śiva.

items.question: What is heard abiding in the ear and come down through tradition?
premises: It is heard abiding in the ear.
It has come down through tradition.
items.inference: The teaching is heard in the ear and transmitted through tradition.
uncertainties: The exact antecedent of the heard teaching is not explicit.
items.plain_english: O goddess, it is heard abiding in the ear, come down through tradition.

items.question: What is accomplished by this mere knowledge that has been heard?
premises: It is addressed to the fair-faced one.
items.inference: The verse emphasizes accomplishment through mere heard knowledge.
uncertainties: The main verb is omitted or implied in the verse.
items.plain_english: By this mere knowledge, heard, O fair-faced one.
